title: Supporting Digital Skills for Next Generation
description: The project aims to strengthen digital education in Zambia by piloting a hub school model in Lusaka Province. The initiative focuses on building teachers' and learners' digital capacity, equipping the school with modern technologies, and ensuring equitable access, especially for girls and disadvantaged groups. It will map existing digital initiatives, draw lessons from successful African models like Ghana, and generate evidence to guide national policy. Key outputs include a computer lab, smart classrooms, digital pedagogy training, and locally relevant learning content. At the national level, the project will contribute to developing a coordinated digital education strategy, ensuring that the pilot serves both as an immediate benefit for the hub school and a proof of concept for scaling up sustainable, cost-effective digital learning solutions across Zambia.

title: Misean Cara core funding — digital literacy in six Zambian schools

title: ZamStats: Increased availability of relevant statistics, 2025-2028 (via the Ministry of Finance, Zambia)
description:
Support to ZamStats to strengthen the management of ZamStats, the coordination of the National Statistical System, methodological capacity in economic, agriculture, environment and social statistics. The capacity building is implemented by Statistics Sweden. Support is also giver to conduct a yearly Household Budget Survey.

Development objective Official statistics is used to design policies for better living conditions in Zambia. Project overall outcome Enhanced capacity to produce statistics in line with user needs, sound statistical methods and international standards. Component outcomes Component 1: Management Component objective/outcome: ZamStats has a leadership team that motivates and supports the staff to successfully adopt change in order to achieve the organisation's goals. Component 2: Coordination Component objective/outcome: A strengthened National Statistical System (NSS) that fosters stronger interagency collaborations to improve data integration, sharing, and dissemination across key government entities. Component 3: Statistical Methodology Component objective/outcome: Enhanced methodological capacity Component 4: Economic Statistics Component objective/outcome: Enhanced capacity for ZamStats to produce timely and relevant economic statistics. Component 5: Agriculture, Environment and Social Statistics Component objective/outcome 1: Agricultural and Environment statistics contributes to evidenced based decision-making on food security in the country. Component objective/outcome 2: Household Budget Survey is produced to inform the users on critical socio-economic, agricultural and environment indicators.

title: Strengthening the National Statistical System of Zambia, 2019-2023 (Statistics Sweden), tranche A0101
description:
The Embassy has received a joint project proposal from Zambia Statistics Agency and Statistics Sweden called "Increased access to statistics that are relevant to meet user needs". The proposal has a total budget of SEK 44 434 000 and is the outcome of a scoping phase implemented by Zamstats and Statistics Sweden between February and July 2019 and financed by the Embassy with a budget of SEK 1 183 000. The proposed contribution is a collaboration between the Zambia Statistics Agency and Statistics Sweden over the period 2019 - 2023. The objective of the project is that users have increased access to unbiased, reliable and quality statistics that are timely, accurate and relevant to meet their needs. The project is divided into four project components. The first component is Coordination and the expected outcome is a strengthened National Statistical System. The second component is Statistical Production and the expected outcome is improved range and quality of Zamstats’ statistical production. The third component is Communication and Dissemination and the expected outcome is increased user access and improved user understanding of existing statistics. The fourth component is Information and Communication Technology and the expected outcome is an ICT environment in place that supports efficient statistics production.

Long-term outcome Increased access to statistics that are relevant to meet user needs. Project Objective Users have increased access to unbiased, reliable and quality statistics that are timely, accurate and relevant to meet user needs. Component outcomes 1. Coordination: The expected outcome of the component is a Strengthened National Statistical System (NSS). 2. Statistical production: Improved range and quality of ZamStats statistical production. 3. Communication and dissemination: Increased user access and improved user understanding of existing statistics 4. Information and Communication Technology (ICT): An ICT environment in place that supports efficient statistics production 5. Management: This component was added in 2023, to enhance change managemnt leadership skills to support the transformation of the agency

title: China Eximbank provides $302 government concessional loan for Phase 2 of the Communication Towers Project
description: In April 2016, the Government of Zambia and Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd. signed an MOU on Phase 2 of the Communication Towers Project. Then, on August 4, 2017, the Chinese Government and the Government of Zambia signed a preferential loan framework agreement for Phase 2 of the Communication Towers Project. On the same day, China Eximbank and the Government of the Republic of Zambia also signed a $302,034,321.68 government concessional loan (GCL) agreement for Phase II of the Smart Zambia National ICT Development Project. The borrowing terms of the GCL are unknown. However, it is known that the borrower was expected to use the proceeds of the loan to finance 100% of the cost of a commercial contract between the Government of Zambia and Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd., which was signed in August 2016. According to Ministry of Transport and Communications of Zambia, by the fourth quarter of 2018, the loan had achieved an 30.3% disbursement rate ($91,637,435.75 out of $302,034,321.68). As of July 2022, the Ministry of Finance & National Planning (MOFNP) of Zambia reported that the loan had achieved an 87.8% disbursement rate ($265,379,267.74 out of $302,034,321.68).   Phase 2 involved the construction of 808 communication towers, 1,009 2G, 3G and 4G wireless stations, as well as the installation of a matched transmission network and user access terminals in unserved and under-served areas. The broad objective is to improve communication services and reach 92 percent network coverage countrywide. Another objective is to ensure that 40 percent of the country has access to data services (from a baseline level of 5 percent). The targets of these communication towers will be relatively population dense villages and economically active areas like hospitals, schools, mines, and tourist areas. title: China Development Bank provides $178.5 million loan for Safe City Project
description: In January 2013, Government of Zambia’s Ministry of Home Affairs and ZTE Corporation signed a $210 million commercial contract for the Safe City Project (also known as Phase III of the Public Security Network Project). Then, in September 2013, the then Minister of Home Affairs Edgar Lungu was forced to cancel the $210 million tender awarded to ZTE Corporation to install closed circuit television (CCTV) cameras on the streets of Lusaka after public outcry and allegations of corruption in the bidding process (including potential kickbacks to Patriotic Front officials). Lungu the referred the case to the Anti-Corruption Commission and the Auditor General at the Ministry of Justice for further investigation. Then, on April 14, 2015, Zambia’s Deputy Minister of Home Affairs Colonel Gerry Chanda announced that the Government of Zambia decided to ‘re-table’ the bid. Nearly 18 months later, in October 2016, China Development Bank (CDB) and the Government of Zambia signed a $178.5 million loan agreement for the Safe City Project. The borrowing terms of the loan are unknown. However, it is known that the borrower was expected to use the proceeds of the loan to partially finance a commercial contract between the Government of Zambia’s Ministry of Home Affairs and ZTE Corporation, which was signed in 2016.
